stem:
Match the questions (i, ii, iii, ..) to the section (a, b, c, …) of the pediatric history.

  1. Social history
  2. Review of systems
  3. Family history
  4. Delivery history
  5. Antenatal history
  6. Postnatal history

options.html: What is baby currently feeding on? Do they have 1 wet diaper per feed? Blood in their stool? Difficult to wake?
What is the childcare arrangement? Is there any history of abuse or neglect? What are the parents’ level of education?
What was the gestational age at time of delivery? Mode of delivery? APGAR score? Birth weight?
Are the parents consanguineous? What ethnicity are the parents? Did the parents face the same issue as the baby when they were young?
Did baby have any past illnesses or surgeries or medications? Is baby up to date on vaccinations?
What was the mother’s previous pregnancies like? Did mother have diabetes or hypertension during this pregnancy? What was her GBS status?

answer: The correct answer is A. iii; B i; C iv; D iii; E vi; F v

stem: When writing a pediatric prescription, what five things should be included? (hint: one of them is dosage form)
answer: Dosage form, concentration, dose (mg AND mL), frequency of use, duration. Example: amoxicillin suspension 50mg/ml: 750 mg (15mL) by mouth every 12 hours x 5 days. Note: Taking a patient’s weight (in kg) is very important for proper dosing.

stem:
Match the developmental action to the age at which the lack of the milestone will start to be a red flag:

  1. 4 mo
  2. 9 mo
  3. 15 mo
  4. 18 mo

options.html: Gross motor: inability to walk
Fine motor: hands still fisted
Language: no babbling
Social: no joint attention

answer: A iv; B i; C ii; D iii

options.html: The Nipissing tool is a surveillance form so it is used continuously as a way to monitor the milestone development of low risk infants/children up to 5 years of age.
Cerebral palsy is the most common physical disability in childhood and while it is non-progressive, comorbidities include delays in other domains.

The difference between global developmental delay and intellectual disability is that intellectual disability is diagnosed by the delay of two developmental domains while global developmental delay is diagnosed by and IQ and adaptive functioning <2 SD.
Primitive reflexes (e.g. Moro, palmar grasp, rooting, sucking, stepping) typically disappear by two months.

answer: The correct answer is B. B is true. A is false because the description describes the Rourke Baby Record. Nipissing is actually a screening (not surveillance tool) so it is used when concerns are elicited by surveillance. For C, the descriptions are flipped (e.g it would be correct if global developmental delay is diagnosed by the delay of 2+ domains). For D, primitive reflexes disappear from 4-6 mo.

stem: Which of the following statements is true?

options.html: If an asthmatic patient scores 4-7 on PRAM with FEV1 50-70%, they should be given continuous nebulized salbutamol and ipratropium for 60 minutes as well as IV steroids and magnesium sulfate.
The three most common causes of bacterial pneumonia is H. influenzae, S. aureus, and Mycoplasma pneumoniae.
Bronchiolitis is most commonly caused by parainfluenza types 1 and 3. Symptoms include inspiratory stridor. It’s treated with oral dexamethasone (and nebulized epinephrine if severe).
Inhaled ipratropium bromide should be added to even mild asthma exacerbations (PRAM 0-3; FEV1 >70%).
Daily inhaled corticosteroids should be prescribed if patients have asthma symptoms (or waking up due to asthma) 2 times per month or more.

answer: The correct answer is E. E is correct. A describes what to do with a “severe asthma exacerbation” (PRAM 8-12, FEV1 <50%). B is incorrect because Strep pneumoniae is the most common cause. C describes croup. D - inhaled ipratropium bromide is only considered when PRAM reaches 6.

stem: List three conditions on your differential diagnosis if a young child presents with a wheeze.
answer: Accepted answers: viral bronchiolitis, asthma, pneumonia, laryngotracheomalacia, foreign body aspiration, GERD, CHF, vascular ring, allergies, CF, mediastinal mass, tracheoesophageal fistula.

options.html: Spanking is a proven method of managing aggressive tantrums in children.
Infant colic follows the rule of 4s: last more than 4 hrs/day, more than 4 days/week, for more than 4 weeks (or a month), peaks at 4 weeks of age.
Proven methods of dealing with infant colic include formula changes and the use of pacifiers.
Pediatric anxiety can present with headaches, blushing, palpitation and muscle tension.

answer: The correct answer is D. D is correct. B is incorrect because infant colic follows the rule of 3s and peaks at 6 weeks of age. C is incorrect because there are no proven methods to dealing with infant colic.

options.html: Most oppositional behaviours (such as tantrums) are unresponsive to behavioural management, such as positive reinforcement.
Night terrors occur during the first ⅓of the night, while nightmares occur in the last ⅓ of the night.
Stimulants that are effective for ADHD include methylphenidate, amphetamine, atomoxetine, and guanificine.
Infantile colic should not be accompanied with a failure to thrive.

answer: A is false because oppositional behaviours are responsive to behavioural management so it is important to praise positive behaviour, teach children how to vent appropriately, and to ignore attention-seeking tantrums.
